title: Quick Tri-Dal
subtitle: A light, everyday tempered dal — toor, urad, and chana, no soaking required.
protein: ~10–12g protein per adult serving — from toor, urad & chana dal

method.title: Rinse and pressure-cook the dals
items: Rinse toor dal {¾ cup}, urad dal {½ cup}, and chana dal {¼ cup} together under water until it runs mostly clear — no soaking needed
Add to the pressure cooker with water {4 cups}, turmeric {¾ tsp}, and salt {1 tsp}
Pressure cook 6–7 whistles on medium heat — the extra whistle or two makes up for skipping the soak, especially for the chana dal
Let pressure release naturally, then whisk lightly with a ladle until the dal is smooth but still has a little texture

method.label: Toddler — pull before the tempering
items: Scoop out a small bowl (about ¾ cup) of the plain cooked dal now, before tempering
Stir in a small pat of ghee {½ tsp} for richness — her bowl stays plain and mild since it's set aside before the chili-spiced tempering is made
Set the bowl aside

method.title: Make the tempering (tadka)
items: Heat ghee {2½ tbsp} in a small pan over medium heat
Add mustard seeds {½ tsp} and let them pop
Add cumin seeds {1 tsp}, sizzle 10 seconds
Add hing {¼ tsp} and grated ginger {1 tbsp}, sauté 20–30 seconds until fragrant
Add Kashmiri chili powder {1 tsp}, stir for just a few seconds so it doesn't scorch

method.title: Combine and finish the adult portion
items: Pour the hot tempering over the remaining dal (the toddler portion has already been set aside) and stir well
Adjust consistency with water as needed — this dal should be pourable, not thick like a gravy
Simmer 3–4 minutes on low heat so the flavors settle
Stir in lemon juice {1½ tbsp} and adjust salt to taste
Garnish with chopped cilantro {2 tbsp} just before serving

method.title: Cool and store for meal prep
items: Let the dal cool to room temperature before refrigerating
Store in an airtight container — keeps well for 4 days refrigerated
Reheat on the stovetop with a splash of water to loosen, and add the cilantro garnish fresh after reheating rather than storing it mixed in

method.label: Notes
method.text: Stovetop pressure cooker works straight from rinsed dal — no soak needed since these are all split and dehusked; give it one or two extra whistles versus a soaked-dal recipe to make sure the chana dal fully softens. Chana dal is optional — skip it and use 1 cup toor dal + ½ cup urad dal instead (same total volume), dropping back to 5–6 whistles. This is a thinner, everyday dal, not a gravy — meant for rice or roti as a daily-rotation option alongside the richer dal makhani. Ginger is added generously here since it's the main warming element doing the work onion and garlic would otherwise do in a lighter dal like this.
